description:
Goal
Make native/codegen respect the settled scalar runtime representation on the map fixture path so codegen never asks for a raw ABI lane that contradicts the value's known runtime kind.

Problem being fixed
The widened native-program suite still fails on the map fixture after fz-hwn.6. The crash is no longer about callable transport; it is a scalar representation mismatch during native codegen.

Verified failure
- `cargo test compiler2_native_program_jit_runs_map_fixture_through_compiler2_codegen --lib -- --nocapture`
- Panic: `known scalar kind does not match requested raw ABI repr`
- The failure happens in native codegen after lowering, which means the settled transport facts and the requested ABI repr disagree.

What we know
- This is a real compiler bug, not stale test drift.
- The failure appears after the transport model changes, so some native/codegen path is still re-litigating representation instead of consuming the settled value/layout facts.
- The right fix is data-model driven: identify where a boxed/scalar value's known kind becomes inconsistent with the requested raw ABI lane, then remove the re-interpretation.

Design rule
- Once native lowering has chosen the scalar representation for a lane, codegen must consume that representation directly.
- No later path may request a narrower raw ABI repr than the settled value kind can support.
- Do not paper over the mismatch with fallback boxing/unboxing shims.

Code seams
- `src/compiler2/jobs/native.rs`
- `src/compiler2/native_codegen/*`
- scalar repr / ABI coercion helpers around the map fixture path

Checks
- `cargo test compiler2_native_program_jit_runs_map_fixture_through_compiler2_codegen --lib`
- no `known scalar kind does not match requested raw ABI repr` panic
- no regression in the focused `.6` spawn/omitted/direct-callable checks
title: Compiler2 native map fixture requests an impossible raw ABI repr
